about.title: The MakerLAB at Cornell Tech
about.lede: A place where anyone at Cornell Tech can take an idea from a first sketch to a working prototype.
about.labBody: The MakerLAB is Cornell Tech's makerspace: an accessible production hub with the tools to prototype and build. Students get hands-on experience solving real problems, startups refine their products, and faculty build prototypes for their research. It has a wood shop for large builds and assembly, a laser room for cutting and engraving, and an electronics lab.
about.historyBody: The lab started in 2016 with two machines, a laser cutter and a 3D printer, and grew from there. Its new home on the first floor of the Tata Innovation Center opened on May 2, 2025.
about.where: First floor, Tata Innovation Center, Cornell Tech, 2 West Loop Road, Roosevelt Island, New York, NY 10044
about.hours: Access holders: 8 AM to 8 PM, seven days a week. Super Makers, who apply for it, have access around the clock.
about.hoursNote: Hours and access can change: the official MakerLAB page has the current ones and how to apply.
about.communityBody: Through CRAFT@Large, the MakerLAB's community initiative, organizations across New York City can propose projects that need digital fabrication and make them with the lab.
about.projectBody: MakerLAB Tools is the lab's digital guide: every machine and hand tool in one catalog, with which units are free, the manuals, the safety requirements and the training each one needs. Inside it is MakerLAB AI, an AI that knows the lab's real inventory. Ask it to help you:
about.operateBody: How do I use this machine?
about.debugBody: Something went wrong — what should I check?
about.createBody: I have an idea. How could I make it with the machines here?
about.assistantLimits: It answers from the catalog and each tool's manuals, says so when it doesn't know, and sends you to MakerLAB staff for safety questions, access and training sign-offs.
about.whyBody: It was built so that anyone can find the right machine and learn how to use it safely before they walk over, in their own language.
about.creditsBody: Built by Isaac Steinberg (Tech Lead, Johnson Cornell Tech MBA '26) for the MakerLAB, which Niti Parikh (Director) and Luis Rodrigo Navarro (Assistant Director) run.
about.feedbackBody: If you spot a mistake, use "Report a correction" on the tool's page — corrections go to the staff queue and are fixed in the app. For a broken machine, use Report in the header.
about.mcpBody: The catalog is also available to AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Codex over MCP, at this site's /api/mcp address. Browsing needs no account. To let an assistant file reports as you, with your role's permissions and nothing more, sign in with Google from the assistant; a personal access token is there for clients that can't.
about.mcpLink: See the MCP server and its tools
about.usageBody: To improve the lab, we keep anonymous usage counts — which tools and manuals are asked about and which questions go unanswered — never who asked.

formulas.heading: How these numbers are calculated
formulas.questions: Questions answered = {app} assistant questions in the app + {mcp} over MCP ({lookups} catalogue lookups by outside assistants ÷ {perQuestion} lookups per question, rounded down) = {total}.
formulas.questionsNoMcp: Questions answered = {app} assistant questions in the app. MCP lookups by outside assistants ({lookups}) are not counted, as the lab chose.
formulas.handled: Handled without staff = {app} app questions − {unanswered} the assistant could not answer ({kinds}) + {mcp} MCP questions = {handled}, or {share} of questions. MCP has no “could not answer” signal, so every MCP question counts as handled.
formulas.handledNoMcp: Handled without staff = {app} app questions − {unanswered} the assistant could not answer ({kinds}) = {handled}, or {share} of questions.
formulas.hours: Staff hours saved ≈ {handled} handled questions × {minutes} minutes a staff member would otherwise spend ÷ 60 = {hours} hours.
formulas.value: Estimated value ≈ {hours} hours × {cost} loaded staff cost per hour = {value}.
formulas.afterHours: Outside staffed hours = {after} of {total} questions were asked when staff are not in ({staffed}, {timeZone}) = {share}. Hours are counted in lab time, so daylight saving moves nothing.
formulas.note: Every count is anonymous: questions are counted, never stored with who asked. Staff testing is left out. Counts can be low (a blocked request, a failed write), never high.

aiPrompt.label: setup prompt
aiPrompt.signInText:
Connect yourself to the MakerLAB Tools MCP server so you can look up the lab's equipment for me.

1. Add a remote MCP server named "makerlab" (HTTP transport) at this sign-in address: {signedInUrl}
   It uses OAuth: I'll be sent to my browser to sign in with Google and approve the connection. No token is needed.
2. Only if you can't sign in that way: use {url} instead, with the header "Authorization: Bearer ${envVar}", reading the token from the {envVar} environment variable at run time. Never ask me to paste the token into this chat, and never print it or write it into a file.
3. Once connected, list the MakerLAB tools you can use and tell me which ones need me signed in.

If you can't add MCP servers yourself, tell me the exact steps to do it in this app instead.
aiPrompt.tokenText:
Connect yourself to the MakerLAB Tools MCP server so you can look up the lab's equipment for me.

I've made a personal access token and put it in the {envVar} environment variable.

2. Send the header "Authorization: Bearer ${envVar}", reading the value from the {envVar} environment variable at run time. Never ask me to paste the token into this chat, and never print it or write it into a file — refer to the variable instead.

product.pillarsLede: Three kinds of question, one AI. Each answer below is real, from the X1-Carbon's page on the live site.

operate.label: Operate
operate.question: What does the quick start guide say about the first print?
operate.body: How to use a machine, step by step, from its own manual, with the page it came from.
operate.alt: The assistant's answer about the X1-Carbon's first print: four steps from the quick start guide, citing page 8.

debug.label: Debug
debug.question: My first layer isn't sticking to the build plate. What should I check?
debug.body: What to check when something goes wrong, what not to force, and when to stop and get staff.
debug.alt: The assistant's answer about first-layer adhesion: plate, slicer plate type, bed levelling, material settings, then ask staff.

create.label: Create
create.question: I want to print a two-colour phone stand. Which printer, and what settings?
create.body: From an idea to the right machine in this lab, the material, and the settings to start from.
create.alt: The assistant recommends the X1-Carbon with its AMS for a two-colour phone stand, PLA, and how to assign colours in Bambu Studio.

toolPages.title: A page for every tool
toolPages.body: Every tool in the lab has a page: what it does, the training and PPE it needs, the emergency stop, specs and materials, the SOP and manuals, and every physical unit with its status and location. Scan the QR label on a machine to land on its page. Staff print the labels from the inventory, at the sticker size they use, and anyone can save a tool’s code from its page or ask MakerLAB AI for it.
toolPages.alt: The X1-Carbon's tool page with its safety panel, details, documents and units.

citations.title: Answers you can check
citations.body: The assistant searches each machine's manual, page by page, and links the exact pages it used. Tap a page reference to open the manual there. When the manual doesn't cover a question, it says so instead of guessing.
citations.alt: An answer about replacing the Form 4's resin tank, with page references 38 and 20 and a list of the two manual pages it used.

intake.title: Add equipment from a photo or a list
intake.body: Staff photograph a machine or paste an inventory list. The assistant identifies each item, then researches it in the background: the manufacturer's page, specs, the manual and a clean product photo. Nothing is published until a staff member reviews and approves it.
intake.alt: The review page for a researched Prusa MK4S: identified name and brand, a high-confidence grade with its reasons and sources, and the proposed record.

tickets.title: Maintenance tickets from the chat
tickets.body: Tell the assistant a machine is broken. It helps you try the obvious fix first, then files a ticket in the maintenance queue with the machine, the unit and a priority. Staff see it at once, and the lab screen counts it until it's resolved.
tickets.alt: A chat on the Trotec Speedy 400's page: the assistant suggests checking the focus, then files a high-priority ticket.

kiosk.title: A lab status screen
kiosk.body: Open /kiosk on the TV or an iPad at the door: machines that are down, open tickets, today's hours and a featured tool. It refreshes itself, and its QR code opens the assistant on a visitor's phone.
kiosk.alt: The lab status screen: three machines with units down, 13 open tickets, the hours, a QR code and a featured tool.

projects.title: A projects gallery
projects.body: Students submit what they made, with photos and the tools they used. Staff approve each project before it's public, and every tool page shows the projects made with it.
projects.alt: The projects gallery: student projects with photos and the tools used.

insights.title: Usage insights and a value report
insights.body: Which tools people ask about, which they never do, the busiest hours, and the questions the assistant couldn't answer, so staff can add the missing manual. The value report turns this into staff hours saved and after-hours coverage, on one printable page for whoever funds the lab.
insights.alt: The value report: questions answered, the share handled without staff, staff hours saved, estimated value and questions asked outside staffed hours, with each formula written out.

actions.title: Anything the admin screens do, from a sentence
actions.body: Staff can ask the assistant to resolve a ticket, publish a tool, add a unit or approve intake. It prepares the change on a card that shows exactly what will change, and nothing happens until you press Confirm. It acts with your permissions, never more.
actions.never: It never touches the super admin role, removes people, blocks addresses, handles secrets, deployments or backups, shows anyone's full email address, or sends email.
actions.alt: A confirmation card in the chat: update the ticket “Laser bed out of focus”, status open to resolved, with the resolution note, and Confirm and Dismiss buttons.

mcp.body: Claude, ChatGPT and other assistants can use the same catalog over MCP. Browsing needs no account. Sign in with Google from the assistant and it can file reports as you, with your role's permissions.
mcp.alt: The MCP server page: the address to add, how to sign in, and every tool the server offers.

costs.compare: An agent looking things up costs more than a chat because it reads pages: about 5¢ to research a tool against a fraction of a cent to answer a question. That is why research runs only when staff ask for it.
costs.footnote: Measured with the Vercel AI Gateway's reported costs. Estimates, not quotes; prices change.

privacy.signIn: Signing in uses your Cornell Google account. Anyone can browse and ask; signing in unlocks reporting as yourself, the floor map and staff tools.
privacy.usage: Usage is counted anonymously: which tools and manuals are asked about, and which questions go unanswered. Nothing records who asked.
privacy.permissions: The assistant acts only with your permissions and asks before any change. Typing “yes” doesn't confirm anything; the Confirm button does.
privacy.safety: For safety, access and training sign-offs it sends you to MakerLAB staff. It isn't a substitute for a checkout.

quickStartPage.metaDescription: Eight steps to MakerLAB Tools and its assistant: ask about a machine, follow a manual citation, report a problem, add equipment, set up the lab screen and connect your own AI.
quickStartPage.title: Quick start
quickStartPage.lede: What's there, what to try, and how to use it. Steps 1–4 and 8 work for anyone; 5–7 are for MakerLAB staff.

open.title: Open the site
open.body: Go to makerlab-ai.vercel.app on a laptop or phone. Every tool in the lab is there: search, filter by category or status, or press ⌘K (Ctrl K) to jump to one. No account needed.
open.alt: The tools gallery: a search box, filters and tool cards with photos.

ask.title: Ask the assistant on a tool page
ask.body: Open the Bambu Lab X1-Carbon and press the orange button at the bottom right. Ask “How do I start a print with the AMS?”, or “What does the quick start guide say about the first print?” (shown here). The assistant knows which machine you're looking at, so you don't have to name it.
ask.alt: The assistant's answer on the X1-Carbon's page, citing the quick start guide.

cite.title: Follow a manual citation
cite.body: When an answer comes from a manual, it shows page references like “p. 38” and lists the pages under the answer. Tap one to open the manual at that page and check it yourself.
cite.alt: An answer with page references and the list of manual pages it used.

report.title: Report a problem
report.body: Tell the assistant what's wrong, or press Report in the header. It suggests the obvious checks first, then files a ticket for the right machine. Sign in so staff know who reported it.
report.alt: The assistant files a maintenance ticket for the Trotec Speedy 400.

intake.title: Add a tool from a photo
intake.body: Sign in with your Cornell Google account and open Admin → Intake. Press Ask the assistant, attach a photo of the machine (or an inventory list) and say “add this”. Check the name it identified, then press Research selected. Research runs in the background; when the item is ready, open it on Intake, review the proposed record and approve it.
intake.alt: An intake item ready for review, with its confidence grade, sources and proposed record.

people.title: Give people roles and titles
people.body: Admin → People lists everyone who has signed in. A super admin sets each person's role (User, Admin, Super admin) and a title such as Director or SuperMaker. Roles decide what they can do; titles are what others see.
people.alt: The People page: the roster with roles and titles.

kiosk.title: Set up the lab screen
kiosk.body: Open /kiosk on the TV's browser and make it full-screen. On an iPad: open it in Safari, Add to Home Screen, turn on Guided Access and set Auto-Lock to Never. It needs no sign-in and refreshes on its own.
kiosk.alt: The lab status screen with machines down, open tickets and a QR code.

mcp.title: Connect Claude or ChatGPT
mcp.body: Open /mcp for the address to add to your assistant as an MCP server. It can browse the catalog straight away; sign in with Google when it asks, and it can file reports as you.
mcp.alt: The MCP page with the server address and its tools.

assistantPage.title: What MakerLAB AI can and can't do
assistantPage.lede: MakerLAB AI is the chat on every page. It is offered exactly what your account could do by hand, never more — and some things it never does for anyone. This page is built from the same definitions the assistant runs on, so it can't fall out of date.
assistantPage.forYouHeading: What it can do for you
assistantPage.forYou: {role, select, anonymous {You're not signed in.} user {You're signed in as a lab member.} admin {You're signed in as an admin.} other {You're signed in as a super admin.}} Your column is highlighted below.
assistantPage.forYouCounts: In the chat, MakerLAB AI can do {reads, plural, one {# kind of lookup} other {# kinds of lookup}} and file {records, plural, one {# kind of report} other {# kinds of report}} for you, and prepare {proposes, plural, =0 {no changes} one {# kind of change} other {# kinds of change}} for you to confirm.
assistantPage.forYouCare: Of those changes, {spend, plural, one {# spends} other {# spend}} research credits and {typedName, plural, one {# can't} other {# can't}} be undone.
assistantPage.signInHint: Signing in unlocks reporting as yourself and seeing your own reports; staff get the admin tools.
assistantPage.matrixLede: One row per thing it can do. The four middle columns are the chat, by role; the last is an outside AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex…) connected to the lab's MCP server as a person of that role.

legend.propose: Prepares a change on a card; nothing changes until you press Confirm
legend.mcpInbox: MCP: stores a proposal in your inbox (/admin/proposals, 7 days)

flags.typedName: can't be undone — type the name to confirm
flags.notAfterOutside: not in a message that read outside text
flags.notSuperAdmin: User ↔ Admin only; never super admin

assistantPage.pageOnlyNote: Staff do this on its page; the assistant doesn't offer it.
assistantPage.neverHeading: Never, on any surface, whatever your role
assistantPage.neverLede: Not in the chat, not over MCP, not for a super admin. People who hold the permission still do these in the app by hand.

confirm.card: It never makes a change itself. It puts a card in front of you showing exactly what will change, read from the database, and the change happens only when you press Confirm. Typing “yes” confirms nothing.
confirm.recheck: Confirming checks your permission and every rule again, just as the button on the page would. If the record changed since the card was drawn, nothing is saved.
confirm.expiry: Cards expire after an hour. Proposals from an outside AI wait in Assistant proposals (/admin/proposals) for 7 days, where only you can confirm them.
confirm.outside: After it reads outside text in a message — a web page, a manual, a ticket, an imported list — it won't prepare changes to people or anything that can't be undone until you ask again in a new message.
confirm.reports: Reports it files for you (a maintenance problem, a correction, a draft, a field change with sources) go to staff to act on; they don't change what the catalog shows.

never.super_admin: Make someone a super admin, or change a super admin's role
never.super_adminWhy: The lab's top access stays a person's decision, on the People page.
never.people_grant_allowanceWhy: They spend the lab's money; granted on the People page.
never.people_removeWhy: Removing a person is done on the People page.
never.people_block_emailWhy: Blocking is done on the People page.
never.people_unblock_emailWhy: Unblocking is done on the People page.
never.mirror_disconnectWhy: It deletes a stored secret; done on the mirror page.
never.category_secrets: Read or set secrets or environment variables
never.category_secretsWhy: A secret must never enter a model's context.
never.category_tokens: Create access tokens or answer a sign-in consent screen
never.category_tokensWhy: Credentials and consent are your own act.
never.category_hosting: Deploy, or change hosting, domains or DNS
never.category_hostingWhy: Hosting is the maintainers' job, outside the app.
never.category_database: Run SQL or touch the database directly
never.category_databaseWhy: Every change goes through the same checks as the buttons.
never.category_backupsWhy: Moving data in bulk is an operator's job.
never.category_audit: Edit or delete the audit trail
never.category_auditWhy: The record of who changed what has to stay trustworthy.
never.category_messagingWhy: It never speaks for the lab outside the app.
never.category_exportWhy: Addresses stay masked; nothing exports them in bulk.
never.category_people: Block, ban or grant allowances under any other name
never.category_peopleWhy: The words themselves are refused, so a new tool can't slip through.

unsubscribe.confirmScope: Only this email stops. Nothing else about your account changes.
unsubscribe.failed: That didn't save. Try again in a moment.

done.ticketFiled: You won't get an email when someone reports a problem with a machine.
done.maintenanceDue: You won't get the morning maintenance reminder.

unsubscribe.doneUndo: Tickets and tasks still show in the app. To get these emails again, ask a lab director.
unsubscribe.invalidBody: It may be incomplete or out of date. Nothing was changed. If you keep getting emails you don't want, ask the lab's staff.
unsubscribe.rateLimitedBody: Too many requests came from this connection. Wait an hour, then open the link again.
